title: Getting Started
text: SeverityEstimate fits Bayesian model estimate infection fatality ratio (IFR) symptomatic infection rate (SIR) case line list data, accounting fact active passive surveillance systems detect cases different rates different symptom profiles. model based Lessler et al. (2016). package uses pipeline API similar spirit tidymodels: first build configure SeverityEstimateModel object, call fit() run Stan sampler obtain SeverityEstimateFit estimates extracted.
code: options(mc.cores = 1L) library(SeverityEstimate) #> Loading required package: checkmate #> Loading required package: rstan #> Loading required package: StanHeaders #>  #> rstan version 2.32.7 (Stan version 2.32.2) #> For execution on a local, multicore CPU with excess RAM we recommend calling #> options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores()). #> To avoid recompilation of unchanged Stan programs, we recommend calling #> rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE) #> For within-chain threading using `reduce_sum()` or `map_rect()` Stan functions, #> change `threads_per_chain` option: #> rstan_options(threads_per_chain = 1)

title: Getting Started
text: modelling workflow two stages. First, SeverityEstimateModel constructed specifying line list, population table, model configuration. set_* call adds one piece configuration returns model calls can chained. set_active_prior/passive_asymptomatic_prior/passive_symptomatic_prior: Set Beta distribution priors surveillance detection rate. use weakly informative prior active detection priors reflect expectation passive surveillance likely capture symptomatic asymptomatic cases. set_strata: Declares column used stratification. Use degrees_of_freedom = 0L unsmoothed categorical effect, provide explicit levels plus degrees_of_freedom > 0L smoothed ordered effect across levels. set_timesteps: Declares column identifies time period observation. set_detection: Maps values detection column canonical types active passive expected model. set_outcome: Maps values outcome column canonical types asymptomatic, symptomatic, severe expected model. configured, fit() samples package’s precompiled Stan model, passing additional arguments (e.g. chains, iter) rstan::sampling(). settings intentionally small keep vignette reasonably quick render. sufficient assess convergence support serious inference. practice ’d want use chains iterations review usual Stan diagnostics.
code: population <- strata[, c("age", "population")]  model <- SeverityEstimateModel(linelist, population) |>   set_active_prior(alpha = 1.0, beta = 1.0) |>   set_passive_asymptomatic_prior(alpha = 1.0, beta = 3.0) |>   set_passive_symptomatic_prior(alpha = 3.0, beta = 1.0) |>   set_strata(     "age",     levels = strata[, "age"],     degrees_of_freedom = 1L   ) |>   set_timesteps("time") |>   set_detection(     "detection",     map = c("Active" = "active", "Passive" = "passive")   ) |>   set_outcome(     "outcome",     map = c(       "Asymptomatic" = "asymptomatic",       "Symptomatic" = "symptomatic",       "Death" = "severe"     )   )  estimate <- fit(   model,   chains = 1L,   iter = 250L,   seed = 123L,   refresh = 0 ) #> Warning: The largest R-hat is NA, indicating chains have not mixed. #> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See #> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#r-hat #> Warning: Bulk Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior means and medians may be unreliable. #> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See #> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#bulk-ess #> Warning: Tail Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior variances and tail quantiles may be unreliable. #> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See #> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#tail-ess
